title: Nintendo Platforming Foundations
blurb: Nintendo EAD's own console-defining leap into 3D, joined by Rare's run of technically dazzling platformers built for the same hardware.

games.title: Super Mario 64
games.blurb: The launch title that invented the 3D platformer template almost overnight, with Europe following about nine months after Japan and North America's 1996 debut.

games.title: Banjo-Kazooie
games.blurb: A collectathon that pushed the N64's texture and draw-distance limits further than almost anything before it, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Banjo-Tooie
games.blurb: A larger, more interconnected sequel with sprawling worlds that load without a break, released across all three regions in 2000.

games.title: Donkey Kong 64
games.blurb: A five-character collectathon so item-dense it shipped with its own Expansion Pak requirement, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Yoshi's Story
games.blurb: A storybook-styled platformer built around Yoshi's fruit-eating and melody collecting, with a distinctly gentler difficulty curve than its SNES predecessor.

games.title: Mischief Makers
games.blurb: A frantic side-scrolling shake-em-up from Treasure — one of the platform's more unusual releases, and one that never received a European release at all.

games.title: Rocket: Robot on Wheels
games.blurb: An inventive, underappreciated platformer from the studio that would later create the Infamous series, built around a robot juggling amusement-park guests.

games.title: Conker's Bad Fur Day
games.blurb: A crude-humor platformer arriving very late in the N64's life, released across all three regions in 2001 just before the system's twilight.

games.title: Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards
games.blurb: Kirby's only N64 outing, introducing power-combining abilities — released in Japan and North America but never given a European cartridge release.

title: Action & Adventure
blurb: Ocarina of Time redefined 3D action-adventure almost on arrival, in a chapter that also holds Rare's most structurally inventive N64 work.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
games.blurb: Widely cited as one of the most influential games ever made, introducing Z-targeting and a day-night cycle — Europe's release followed Japan and North America by a matter of weeks.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask
games.blurb: A darker, three-day-loop sequel reusing Ocarina's engine and character models, released across all three regions in 2000.

games.title: Blast Corps
games.blurb: A demolition-puzzle game about clearing a path for a runaway nuclear missile transport, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Body Harvest
games.blurb: An open-world alien-invasion adventure from the studio that would soon become Rockstar North, released in North America and Europe with no Japanese release.

games.title: Jet Force Gemini
games.blurb: A run-and-gun/adventure hybrid with a squad of three playable characters, released across all three regions in 1999.

games.title: Glover
games.blurb: A physics-driven platformer where the player controls an animated glove rolling a ball through each level, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Mystical Ninja Starring Goemon
games.blurb: Released in Japan the year before under its long-running Ganbare Goemon branding, this action-adventure kept its Japanese-culture setting largely intact for its Western release.

games.title: Space Station Silicon Valley
games.blurb: A body-swapping action-adventure where a robotic hamster possesses the mechanical animals of an abandoned space station, released the same year worldwide.

title: Shooters & FPS
blurb: GoldenEye 007 proved consoles could do first-person shooters on their own terms, in a chapter carrying two of the N64's most-played multiplayer games.

games.title: GoldenEye 007
games.blurb: The console FPS's true breakout moment, built around a four-player split-screen mode that came together almost as an afterthought — released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Perfect Dark
games.blurb: GoldenEye's spiritual successor, requiring the Expansion Pak for its full experience and pushing the engine further with bots and a Combat Simulator mode.

games.title: Star Fox 64
games.blurb: Released across Europe as Lylat Wars rather than Star Fox 64, reportedly to avoid a trademark conflict — the same rail-shooter under a different regional name.

games.title: Doom 64
games.blurb: A ground-up reimagining of the original Doom with new levels and a moodier atmosphere, rather than a straight port — released in North America and Europe with no Japanese release.

games.title: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron
games.blurb: An arcade-style Star Wars flight combat game showing off real-time lighting effects, released in North America in late 1998 with Europe and Japan following into early 1999.

games.title: Quake II
games.blurb: A console conversion of id Software's PC shooter sequel, released across North America and Europe in 1999 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Duke Nukem 64
games.blurb: A heavily censored N64 port of the PC shooter, stripping out blood, nudity and other content to meet Nintendo's policy — released in North America and Europe with no Japanese release.

games.title: Turok: Dinosaur Hunter
games.blurb: One of the N64's earliest FPS releases, built around fog-heavy draw-distance limitations that became part of its distinct look, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Turok 2: Seeds of Evil
games.blurb: A more ambitious sequel requiring the Expansion Pak for its highest visual settings, released the same year worldwide.

title: Role-Playing Adventures
blurb: The N64's cartridge storage kept this the smallest chapter in the collection — a genuine reflection of how much thinner the console's RPG output was next to its disc-based rivals.

games.title: Paper Mario
games.blurb: A flat-paper art style wrapped around turn-based RPG combat, released in Japan in 2000 with North America and Europe following into 2001.

games.title: Quest 64
games.blurb: Released across Europe as Holy Magic Century rather than Quest 64 — one of the platform's clearer EU-exclusive title changes — with all regions releasing in 1998.

games.title: Ogre Battle 64: Person of Lordly Caliber
games.blurb: A tactics-RPG hybrid built around real-time troop movement, released in Japan in 1999 and North America in 2000 — it never received a PAL cartridge release at all, with Europe's first legitimate access coming via a 2010 Wii Virtual Console release.

games.title: Harvest Moon 64
games.blurb: A farming-sim RPG hybrid continuing the series' day-and-season cycle, released in Japan and North America in 1999 with no European release.

games.title: Aidyn Chronicles: The First Mage
games.blurb: One of the last major N64 RPGs, arriving very late in the console's life in North America in early 2001 with Europe following that August — no Japanese release.

games.title: Hybrid Heaven
games.blurb: A genre-blending RPG mixing turn-based wrestling-style combat with exploration, released across all three regions in 1999.

title: Racing
blurb: Mario Kart 64 and F-Zero X anchor a chapter that also holds an oddity: a Namco-published racer that, unlike almost everything else the company made, never reached Japan at all.

games.title: Mario Kart 64
games.blurb: The series' 3D debut, translating Super Mario Kart's Mode 7 tracks into fully polygonal circuits — Europe followed Japan and North America's 1996 launch by several months.

games.title: Diddy Kong Racing
games.blurb: A kart racer with an adventure-mode overworld and vehicle-switching between car, plane and hovercraft, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: F-Zero X
games.blurb: A high-speed sequel trading Mode 7 scaling for a genuinely 3D track engine running at an unusually high frame rate, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Wave Race 64
games.blurb: A jet-ski racer praised for water physics well ahead of its time, released in Japan and North America in 1996 with Europe following into 1997.

games.title: San Francisco Rush
games.blurb: An arcade port built around exaggerated jumps and shortcuts, released in North America and Europe with no Japanese release.

games.title: Top Gear Rally
games.blurb: A rally racer emphasizing car damage modeling, released in North America in 1997 with Europe following into 1998.

games.title: Ridge Racer 64
games.blurb: An unusual case for a Namco arcade franchise: this N64 entry released only in North America and Europe, with no release in Namco's home market of Japan at all.

title: Sports & Extreme
blurb: 1080° Snowboarding and Camelot's Mario sports spin-offs anchor a chapter built around late-90s extreme-sports style as much as competition.

games.title: 1080° Snowboarding
games.blurb: A technically striking snowboarding game praised for its physics and terrain deformation, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Mario Golf
games.blurb: A full 18-hole golf sim wrapped in Mushroom Kingdom characters, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Mario Tennis
games.blurb: A tennis game notable for introducing Waluigi to the Mario cast, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: NFL Blitz
games.blurb: An exaggerated, rules-light arcade football conversion, released across North America and Europe the same year despite its distinctly American sport.

games.title: Beetle Adventure Racing
games.blurb: A Volkswagen Beetle-themed arcade racer built around wide, secret-filled tracks, released across all three regions in 1999.

games.title: Cruis'n Exotica
games.blurb: An arcade racer conversion that, unusually, reached Europe nearly three months before its North American release — no Japanese release.

games.title: Snowboard Kids
games.blurb: A cartoonish snowboarding-kart hybrid that reached the West in 1998 before its Japanese release the following year, an unusual reversal of the platform's typical regional order.

title: Fighting
blurb: Super Smash Bros. debuted here almost as a side project before becoming one of Nintendo's biggest franchises, alongside a chapter full of wrestling and licensed brawlers.

games.title: Super Smash Bros.
games.blurb: The series' debut, built around percentage-based knockback rather than traditional health bars, released in Japan in January 1999 with the West following later that year.

games.title: Killer Instinct Gold
games.blurb: An enhanced N64 port of the arcade fighter adding new characters and combo-training tools, released in North America in 1996 with Europe following into 1997.

games.title: Mortal Kombat Trilogy
games.blurb: A compilation port gathering nearly every character from the series' first three arcade entries onto one cartridge, released in North America in 1996 with Europe following into 1997.

games.title: Fighters Destiny
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Fighting Cup, this point-scoring fighter rewarded ring-outs and style over simple knockouts — an unusual case where the Japanese release reportedly followed the West rather than leading it.

games.title: Clay Fighter 63⅓
games.blurb: A claymation-styled parody fighter released only in North America, with no European or Japanese release.

games.title: WWF No Mercy
games.blurb: Widely regarded as one of the best wrestling games ever made, released across North America and Europe in 2000.

games.title: WWF WrestleMania 2000
games.blurb: A predecessor to No Mercy sharing its acclaimed grapple-based engine, released in Europe in October 1999, days ahead of its North American release, with Japan following nearly a year later.

games.title: Ready 2 Rumble Boxing
games.blurb: An exaggerated arcade boxing game built around cartoonish character designs, released in North America and Europe in 1999 with Japan following into 2000.

games.title: WCW/nWo Revenge
games.blurb: A wrestling game sharing its engine with the WWF titles under a rival promotion's license, released in North America in October 1998 with Europe following about a month later.

title: Puzzle & Party
blurb: Hudson Soft's Mario Party trilogy anchors a chapter of four-player-focused puzzle and board-game hybrids built around the N64's four controller ports.

games.title: Mario Party
games.blurb: The series debut built entirely around its four controller ports, released in Japan and North America in 1998 with Europe following into 1999.

games.title: Mario Party 2
games.blurb: A sequel adding costumed characters and more varied minigame boards, released in Japan and North America in 1999 with Europe following into 2000.

games.title: Mario Party 3
games.blurb: The trilogy's closer, adding a story mode and duel-format minigames, released in Japan and North America in 2000 with Europe following into 2001.

games.title: Bomberman 64
games.blurb: A 3D reinvention of the series mixing platforming stages with the traditional multiplayer arena battles, released in North America and Japan in 1997 with Europe following into 1998.

games.title: Bomberman Hero
games.blurb: A more action-adventure-focused spin-off dropping the traditional battle-arena multiplayer in favor of a linear campaign, released across all three regions around 1998–1999.

games.title: Pokémon Puzzle League
games.blurb: A Pokémon-themed reskin of Tetris Attack's puzzle engine, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Tetrisphere
games.blurb: An unusual spherical take on Tetris built around clearing tiles from a rotating 3D globe, released in North America in 1997 with Europe following into 1998.

games.title: Wetrix
games.blurb: A physics-driven puzzle game about managing rising water on a deforming 3D landscape, released across all three regions in 1998.

title: Simulation & Strategy
blurb: Pokémon Snap and Pokémon Stadium anchor a chapter that also holds SimCity's own sequel — a title that, unusually, never left Japan on this platform at all.

games.title: Pokémon Snap
games.blurb: A rail-shooter-styled photography game built around capturing wild Pokémon on camera, released in Japan and North America in 1999 with Europe following into 2000.

games.title: Pokémon Stadium
games.blurb: A 3D battle simulator letting players import their Game Boy Pokémon into fully rendered arena fights, released the same year across North America and Europe.

games.title: Pokémon Stadium 2
games.blurb: A sequel adding support for the Gold and Silver generation, released in Japan in 2000 with North America and Europe following into 2001.

games.title: SimCity 2000
games.blurb: A city-building sequel adding mini-games and disaster events on top of the original's simulation — a Japan-exclusive N64 release that never reached the West on this platform at all.

games.title: Command & Conquer
games.blurb: A console conversion of the PC real-time strategy landmark, released across North America and Europe in 1999 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Worms Armageddon
games.blurb: A turn-based artillery-strategy hit ported to N64, released in Europe in December 1999 with North America following into early 2000 — no Japanese release.

games.title: Army Men: Sarge's Heroes
games.blurb: A third-person shooter starring green plastic toy soldiers, released across North America and Europe in 1999 with no Japanese release.

title: Licensed, Movie & TV Tie-ins
blurb: LucasArts' pair of Star Wars N64 exclusives anchor a chapter of largely well-regarded licensed titles, including two spy-franchise shooters riding GoldenEye's success.

games.title: Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire
games.blurb: An original Star Wars story filling the gap between The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Star Wars Episode I: Racer
games.blurb: A podracing game built to show off the N64's speed-sensation rendering, released the same year worldwide alongside the film it was based on.

games.title: Spider-Man
games.blurb: A well-regarded web-slinging action game, released in North America and Europe in 2001 with no Japanese release.

games.title: South Park
games.blurb: A crude-humor first-person shooter based on the animated series, released in North America in 1998 with Europe following into 1999.

games.title: 007: The World Is Not Enough
games.blurb: A GoldenEye-styled Bond FPS built by the same genre lineage rather than the same studio, released in North America in October 2000 with Europe following that December — no Japanese release, as with the platform's other Bond titles.

games.title: Batman Beyond: Return of the Joker
games.blurb: An animated-series tie-in platformer, released in North America in late 2000 with Europe following in January 2001 — no Japanese release.

games.title: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue
games.blurb: A well-received platformer built around the film's cast, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Mission: Impossible
games.blurb: A stealth-action title based on the 1996 film, released across North America and Europe in 1998 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Rampage World Tour
games.blurb: An N64-specific port of the giant-monster arcade brawler, built by a different studio than the PlayStation version, released in North America in September 1997 with Europe following that December — no Japanese release.

title: Cult Classics & Deep Cuts
blurb: A trio of celebrated Japan-exclusive titles anchors this chapter — games the West only ever got to experience through much later re-releases on entirely different hardware.

games.title: Sin and Punishment
games.blurb: A rail-shooter/action hybrid from Treasure, released only in Japan — its first official Western release came seven years later via Wii Virtual Console.

games.title: Custom Robo
games.blurb: A robot-battling RPG hybrid that launched a small franchise, Japan-exclusive on N64; the series wouldn't reach the West until later Game Boy Advance and GameCube entries.

games.title: Dōbutsu no Mori (Animal Forest)
games.blurb: The original life-sim that would become Animal Crossing, Japan-exclusive on N64 — its Western debut came via an enhanced GameCube port in 2002 (NA) and 2004 (EU).

games.title: Excitebike 64
games.blurb: A 3D revival of the NES original blending motocross racing with a track-editor mode, released in North America and Japan in 2000 with Europe following into 2001.

games.title: Chameleon Twist
games.blurb: An offbeat platformer starring a tongue-grappling chameleon, released in Japan and North America in 1997 with Europe following into 1998.

games.title: Iggy's Reckin' Balls
games.blurb: A rolling-ball arena platformer released in North America in 1998 with Europe following into 1999 — no Japanese release.

games.title: Bomberman 64: The Second Attack
games.blurb: A story-driven sequel with a notably darker tone than the original, released in Japan and North America in 1999–2000 with no European release.

games.title: Vigilante 8
games.blurb: A vehicular-combat game with a 1970s setting, released in North America and Europe in 1999 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Buck Bumble
games.blurb: An unusual bee-themed flight-combat shooter, released across all three regions in late 1998.

title: Arcade Ports & Multiplayer Curios
blurb: The largest chapter in the collection, gathering Midway's arcade conversions alongside a run of licensed and original multiplayer-focused racers and shooters.

games.title: Cruis'n USA
games.blurb: An early arcade racing port and one of the N64's launch-window titles, released in North America in 1996 with Europe following into 1997 — no Japanese release.

games.title: Rush 2: Extreme Racing USA
games.blurb: A stunt-jump-heavy arcade racing sequel, released across North America and Europe in 1998 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Extreme-G
games.blurb: A high-speed anti-gravity racer from a British studio, released across all three regions in 1997.

games.title: NBA Courtside 2 Featuring Kobe Bryant
games.blurb: A basketball sim built exclusively for the North American market, with no European or Japanese release.

games.title: Wayne Gretzky's 3D Hockey
games.blurb: An arcade-style hockey game released in North America in late 1996 with Europe following into 1997 — Japan's release trailed by over a year.

games.title: Micro Machines 64 Turbo
games.blurb: A British-developed miniature-vehicle racer released across all three regions in 1999.

games.title: GEX 64: Enter the Gecko
games.blurb: A wisecracking platformer starring a gecko television addict, released across North America and Europe in 1998 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Bust-A-Move '99
games.blurb: Released in Europe the year before as Bust-A-Move 3 DX, this puzzle game reached Europe well ahead of its own Japanese (as Puzzle Bobble 64) and North American releases.

games.title: NBA Hangtime
games.blurb: An exaggerated arcade basketball conversion, released in North America in early 1997 with Europe following that September — no Japanese release.

games.title: Automobili Lamborghini
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Super Speed Race 64 through a different publisher, this supercar racer reached North America and Europe first, with Japan following about six months later.

games.title: San Francisco Rush 2049
games.blurb: A futuristic sequel to the Rush arcade series, released across North America and Europe in 2000 with no Japanese release.

games.title: Rampage 2: Universal Tour
games.blurb: A sequel continuing the giant-monster arcade brawler formula, released across North America and Europe in 1999 with no Japanese release.
